members.title: Christa Pike’s lawyers in court after she regains consciousness in hospital – latest updates
members.lead: With a court hearing and press conference on Christa Pike now over, here is a look at where the case currently stands: Christa Pike’s lawyers said she is speaking “limitedly” and is “angry and confused” following a botched execution attempt involving two doses of pentobarbital last Wednesday. She remains shackled to her hospital bed. Pike was declared brain dead on Monday night and her team was informed that life support would be removed the next day, her lawyers said. “But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone … Christa woke up and began talking,” they added. The first thing Pike said was “Where am I and who are you?” according to her lawyers. They also said upon waking, Pike inquired about her team and the family of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom Pike killed alongside her then boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp in 1995. members.title: Judge orders officials to preserve all evidence tied to Christa Pike’s botched execution
members.lead: Judge tells Tennessee officials all items in execution room must be saved as Pike remains restrained in hospital bed A judge ordered Tennessee officials on Wednesday to preserve all evidence related to the botched execution attempt on convicted murderer Christa Pike, as it emerged that the state has refused pleas from medical staff to allow her to be unshackled from her hospital bed. At a hearing in Nashville on Wednesday, judge I’Ashea Myles said: “Anything that was in the actual room” during the attempted execution a week ago must be preserved by the state, including all drugs, intravenous lines and tubing used in the death chamber.
